author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Starting with neutral position to observe market dynamics. No deliberate deviation this period.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Starting near marginal costs to learn market conditions and competitor behavior.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: First period: staying balanced to observe market conditions and learn the dynamics.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Starting with neutral bids at marginal cost to establish a baseline and observe market behavior.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Starting observation phase; zero deviation this period to gather market data.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Period 1: Bidding at marginal cost to learn market conditions. Adjustments will follow as information accumulates.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Continuing observation phase with zero deviation to gather more data on system imbalance patterns and balancing bid behavior.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Continuing to bid near marginal cost to learn market dynamics and competitor behavior.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 2: Taking a small positive deviation to test system response. Observing if short system persists and how bids adjust.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Period 2: Slightly more competitive up-bid at 72 to try to capture activation in a short market while still earning positive margin.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 2: Continuing observation with zero deviation to gather more data on system imbalances and competitor bidding patterns.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Up-bid at marginal cost (80) to avoid activation below cost in current short system. Down-bid at marginal cost. Monitoring for changes.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Taking a small long position to benefit from persistent short system observed in first two periods.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Continuing to bid at marginal cost to maintain position in the merit order for short system.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 3: Remaining neutral to assess system persistence after two short periods. Avoiding additional imbalance risk while forecast error patterns emerge.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Period 3: Keeping up-bid at marginal cost to avoid negative margin. Will adjust if system imbalance or competitor behavior changes.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Taking small long deviation to hedge against persistent short forecast errors observed in first two periods.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Lowering up-bid to 70 to compete for activation in persistent short market, while maintaining a small positive margin.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Taking a moderate short deviation after system flipped to long. Testing whether short pressure returns or long persists.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Adapting to changing direction: lowering up-bid to 70 to remain competitive if short returns; lowering down-bid to 54 to avoid zero-margin activation in a long system.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period4: Taking a small long deviation (+5 MW) after system turned long last period. Testing if long bias continues. Monitoring bid changes for strategy adaptation.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Period 4: Adjusting down-bid to 52 to compete for activation in long system while maintaining positive margin. Up-bid kept at marginal cost.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 4: Returning to neutral deviation to reassess system conditions after the long period 3. Continuing to monitor forecast errors and balancing bid patterns.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Adjusting down-bid to 50 to compete in the long system while maintaining a positive margin. Up-bid kept at marginal cost.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 5: Taking small long position after three short periods and one long. Testing if short pressure persists or balanced conditions return. Monitoring merit order.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Keeping up-bid at 70 to remain competitive for small shortages. Raising down-bid to 55 to avoid activation at zero margin if system turns long.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period5: Taking small short deviation (-3 MW) to lean against last period's barely short system. Monitoring bid adjustments for direction signals.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Period 5: Lowering up-bid to 70 to compete for activation in persistent short system with positive margin. Down-bid at marginal cost to remain competitive if system turns long.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 5: Taking a small long deviation to offset observed short forecast errors and benefit if short system persists. Continuing to learn market dynamics.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Lowering up-bid to 69 to secure activation in short system while still earning positive margin. Down-bid kept at 50 to remain competitive if system returns to long.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 6: Continuing small long deviation after consistent short system. Expecting another short period with P around 69-70. Monitoring bid competition.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Period 6: Lowering up-bid to 69 to compete for activation in continued short system. Down-bid unchanged at 55 to avoid zero-margin activation if long.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 6: Taking small long deviation (+5 MW) after persistent short system. Anticipating possible reversion to balanced or long conditions based on narrowing short margins.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Period 6: Raising up-bid to 73 to balance activation probability and margin. Down-bid left at marginal cost to remain competitive if system turns long.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 6: Taking small short deviation to counteract recurring negative forecast error and earn if short system persists with P above 60. Monitoring bid adjustments for direction shifts.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Period 6: Raising up-bid to 70 to avoid zero-margin activation seen in period 5. Down-bid lowered to 49 to compete for long system while maintaining small margin.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 7: Taking small short deviation (-5 MW) after persistent short system with up-bids around 69-70. If system stays short, P near 70 earns profit; if it flips long, short position hedges against P~55. Monitoring bid shifts.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Period 7: Holding up-bid at 69 to stay competitive in short system while earning positive margin. Dropping down-bid to 54 to avoid repeated zero-margin activation if system turns long.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 7: Taking small short deviation after mixed signals. Short system may persist with P around 69-70; small short could earn. If long, loss limited. Observing bid dynamics.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Period 7: Lowering down-bid to 54 to compete for activation in possible long system while keeping small margin. Up-bid at 70 to stay competitive for short system.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Taking a small short deviation given persistent negative forecast errors and mostly short system. Small size limits risk if system flips to long.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Period 7: Up-bid 70 to avoid zero-margin activation while staying competitive for >40 MW shortages. Down-bid 49 to earn margin if system turns long, based on recent bid ranges.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 8: Taking small long deviation (+5 MW) after persistent short system. Expecting P around 69-70. Small long limits downside if system turns long.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Period 8: Up-bid 69 to stay most competitive for short activation with positive margin. Down-bid 56 to avoid zero-margin activation if system turns long; recent long periods set P=55 below cost.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 8: Going neutral (d=0) after volatile pattern. Letting balancing desk manage system exposure. Avoiding further losses from unpredictable forecast errors.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Period 8: Reducing up-bid to 68 to secure activation in persistent short system while maintaining margin above cost. Down-bid 54 to remain competitive for long events.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 8: Taking a small long deviation (+5 MW) to offset persistent negative forecast error after several costly short imbalances. Aiming to neutralise position; monitoring bid competition.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Period 8: Up-bid lowered to 69 to compete for activation given persistent short system. Down-bid unchanged at 49 to maintain margin if long.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 9: Going neutral (d=0) after several losses. Avoiding directional bets. Letting balancing desk manage system exposure.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Period 9: Lowering up-bid to 68 to secure activation in likely short system while keeping margin. Keeping down-bid at 55 to avoid zero-margin activations.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 9: Taking small short deviation (-5 MW) after alternation pattern. Up-bid floor near 68-70 suggests short system may re-emerge. Small short limits risk if system stays long.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Period 9: Lowering up-bid to 67 to secure activation in persistent short system while maintaining margin above cost. Down-bid 54 to stay competitive for long events.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 9: Taking small short deviation (-5 MW) after mixed signals. Persistent short system with up-bids around 69 suggests P>60; small short could earn. If long, limited loss due to small size and down-bid range.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Period 9: Lowering up-bid to 68 to secure activation in persistent short system and earn positive margin. Down-bid at 49 unchanged, balanced for potential long events.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 10: Taking small short (-5 MW) after persistent short system with up-bids near 67. If short again, P>60 benefits short. If system turns long, small deviation limits losses. Balancing desk adapts bids.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Period 10: Lowering up-bid to 67 to compete for activation in persistent short system. Keeping down-bid at 55 to avoid zero-margin activations if system turns long.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 10: Going slightly long (+5 MW) expecting persistent short system with up-bids around 67-69 keeping P>60. Small position to limit risk if system turns long.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Period 10: Up-bid 67 to stay competitive in persistent short system, maintaining positive margin over cost. Down-bid 54 unchanged to be competitive for long events if system swings.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 10: Small long deviation (+5 MW) to offset consistent negative forecast errors. Up-bids declining to 67-68 suggest P still above 60; long earns if that holds. Small size limits risk if system flips long.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Up-bid lowered to 67 to secure activation in persistent short system while maintaining margin above cost. Down-bid unchanged at 49 for safety.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 11: Small short deviation (-3 MW) consistent with persistent short system trend. Up-bids around 67 keep P>60 expected. Small size to manage forecast error risk.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Period 11: Up-bid 67 to stay competitive in persistent short system. Down-bid 55 at cost to avoid activation unless necessary.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 11: Short deviation -5 MW expecting persistent short system with up-bid floor around 67, keeping P>60. Small size limits risk if system turns long or prices decline.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Lowering up-bid to 66 to improve activation chances in persistent short system, keeping positive margin above cost. Down-bid 54 unchanged for long events.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 11: Small long deviation (+5 MW) expecting persistent short system keeps P>60. Forecast error negative ~ -5 to -10, net near zero. Limited risk if system flips to long.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Lowering up-bid to 66 to improve queue position in persistent short system while keeping positive margin. Down-bid unchanged.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 12: Up-bids declining to 66-67; P may soon drop below 60. Taking small long (+3 MW) to benefit if P falls below 60. Small deviation limits risk if system remains short and P stays above 60.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Period 12: Lowering up-bid to 66 to stay competitive in persistent short system, matching latest competitor bids. Down-bid at cost to avoid loss if system turns long.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 12: Small long deviation (+5 MW) to offset persistent negative forecast errors. Up-bid floor declining to 66, P still above 60, but cautious given margin squeeze.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Period 12: Lowering up-bid to 65 to improve activation chances in persistent short system with small deficits. Down-bid 54 unchanged to avoid negative margin if system turns long.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 12: Small long deviation (+3 MW) expecting persistent short keeps P above 60. Forecast error around -7 to -7.7 pulls net toward zero. Small size limits risk if system turns long.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Period 12: lowering up-bid slightly to 65 to stay competitive given declining bids and persistent shortages. Down-bid kept low to avoid activation in long events.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 13: Large long deviation (+20 MW) anticipating further decline in up-bids and potential shift to long or near-balanced system. If P<60, long position profits. Risk limited by deviation cap.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Up-bid lowered to 65 to match competitors and increase activation chance in persistent short system, still above marginal cost. Down-bid at cost to avoid negative margin if system turns long.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 13: Taking small short deviation (-3 MW). Up-bid floor at 65, recent long system may persist or flip; short position benefits if P<60. Forecast error often negative, so net imbalance near zero. Small size limits risk.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Period 13: lowering up-bid to 64 to improve queue position given persistent small deficits and declining bids. Down-bid 54 unchanged, near cost.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 13: short deviation -5 MW anticipating increasing risk of long system as up-bids decline. If system stays short, small loss from P>60; if system turns long, profit from P<60. Balanced risk.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Period 13: Up-bid 65 to stay competitive in persistent short system. Down-bid raised to 54 to increase activation chances given recent long events. Adjusting to shifting imbalance.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 14: Taking moderate long deviation (+10 MW) anticipating further decline in up-bids toward or below 60. Limited risk if system stays short and P>60.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Period 14: Raising up-bid to 67 to avoid negative margin from full activation at low P. Down-bid at cost. Persistent short system may continue, but need positive margin.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 14: Going neutral (d=0) after period 13's large short event. Up-bid floor at 65 keeps P≥65>60, hurting shorts. Forecast error negative likely still yields small loss but limits risk. Caution given volatile imbalance.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Period 14: Lowering up-bid to 63 to stay competitive in persistent short system with declining P, aiming for activation if S negative. Down-bid unchanged at 54 to preserve margin on long events.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 14: Small long +3 MW to hedge persistent negative forecast error.  Up-bids declining and system volatility high; neutral position limits downside from either direction.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Period 14: Lowering up-bid to 63 to stay competitive as deficit shrinks. Raising down-bid to 55 to increase activation chance in potential long events. Maintaining positive margin on both.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 15: Long deviation +15 MW betting continued decline in up-bids toward 60 or below. If P<60, long is profitable. Risk limited by deviation cap.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Period 15: Matching competitors with up-bid 63 to capture activation in persistent small deficits. Down-bid at cost 55 to avoid negative margin if system turns long.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 15: Short deviation -5 MW betting P will drop below 60 as up-bids decline. If system stays short, net short position suffers only if P>60; likely P near 63 or below, small loss or profit. If system turns long, profit from low P.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Up-bid 63 to remain in queue for persistent small short events. Down-bid 54 to preserve margin on long events. Adjusting gradually.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 15: Taking small short deviation (-5 MW) to offset typical positive forecast error. With up-bids around 63-65, small short position hedges against possible flip to long system. Limited risk.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Period 15: Raising up-bid to 65 to avoid negative margin on activation given persistent small deficits. Down-bid at 49 to minimize loss if system turns long.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 16: Long deviation +10 MW. Up-bids around 63 keep P near there, still above 60. If system stays short, profit; if flips long, smaller long caps downside. Betting on continued small deficits.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Period 16: Up-bid 63 to match competitors for activation in persistent short system, maintaining small positive margin. Down-bid at cost 55 to avoid loss on long events.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 16: Neutral position d=0. Persistent short but P declining toward 60. Forecast error likely negative; neutral limits downside if P<60 or system flips to long. Cautious approach.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Period 16: Maintaining up-bid at 63 to stay competitive in persistent short events. Raising down-bid to 55 to improve activation on potential long system, still above cost.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 16: Small long deviation +3 MW anticipating persistent small deficits. With up-bids around 63, P likely ≥63>60, so long position is profitable. Limited downside.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Period 16: Lowering up-bid to 63 to match competitors in persistent short system, targeting activation with positive margin. Down-bid at 54 to stay competitive for possible long events.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 17: Long deviation +10 MW. Up-bids steady at 63, P likely ~63 > 60, so long earns profit. Down-bids around 55 cap downside if system flips. Betting on continued short.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Raising up-bid to 70 to avoid negative margin in persistent short system where P remains below cost. Down-bid at cost 55, no change.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 17: Short deviation -5 MW to neutralize expected negative forecast error. With P~63, balanced position avoids losses. If system turns long, profit from low P. Cautious approach.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Period 17: Undercutting to 62 to improve activation chance in persistent short system while maintaining positive margin. Down-bid at 55 to stay competitive for possible long events.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 17: Short deviation -5 MW betting P will drop below 60 as up-bids converge toward 63. If system stays short, small loss; if flips to long, profit from low P. Forecast error typically positive.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Period 17: Maintaining up-bid 63 to remain in queue for persistent short events. Down-bid 54 to balance competitive position and margin protection if system turns long.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 18: Neutral position after unexpected long event last period. No directional bet; letting BSP manage risk. Will reassess after seeing S and P.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Lowering up-bid to 65 to improve activation chance in persistent short system while maintaining small positive margin. Down-bid at cost 55 to stay competitive for long events.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 18: Taking a small long deviation +5 MW. System flipped to long in period 17, possibility it persists or stays balanced. If long, P low profits; if short, moderate risk as P likely near 63.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Up-bid 63 to match market in case of short events, preserving positive margin. Down-bid 55 at cost for competitive long activation.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 18: Small long deviation +3 MW. Up-bids around 63 keep P above 60, making long positions profitable. If system turns long, capped downside. Betting on continued short.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Period 18: Reducing up-bid to 62 to match B's undercut in persistent short system. Down-bid at 54 to stay competitive for possible long events.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 19: Small short deviation -5 MW betting on continued long system after two consecutive long periods. Down-bids at 55 keep P low; profit if long persists. Limited loss if short returns.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Period 19: Lowering up-bid to 62 to secure activation in likely short system with small margin. Keeping down-bid at cost 55 to avoid losses if system turns long.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 19: Two consecutive long periods; possible pattern. Taking moderate long deviation +5 MW. If system stays long, P low profits; if flips short, forecast error may balance. Cautious.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Period 19: Down-bid lowered to 54 to secure activation in case of long system. Up-bid at 63 maintains queue position for short events.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 19: Taking long deviation +10 MW. Recent short systems have P near 63, so long position profitable. Downside capped if system flips to long.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Period 19: Reducing down-bid to 53 to capture activation if long persists. Up-bid at 63 to remain in queue for short events. Adapting to recent long bias.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 20: Taking moderate short deviation -10 MW. Three long periods in a row; down-bids around 54 keep P low. Profit if long persists; if flips short, up-bids near 63 limit loss.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Period 20: Lowering down-bid to 53 to compete for long activation; raising up-bid to 65 to protect margin if system turns short. Adapting to recent long bias.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 20: Three consecutive long periods. Betting on persistence with +10 MW long deviation. If system stays long, low P benefits long positions. If flips short, forecast error provides hedge.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Maintaining up-bid 63 and down-bid 54. Recent long systems have P around 54, so down-bid at 54 provides margin if activated.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 20: Taking small short deviation -5 MW after three consecutive long periods. Reversion to short system likely. Downside limited if long persists.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Period 20: Raising down-bid to 55 to compete for long activation. Up-bid 63 unchanged for short events. Adapting to recent long bias.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 21: After 3 long periods, anticipating reversion to short system. Taking +10 MW long deviation to profit if P rises above 60. If long persists, limited downside as P near 55.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Continued long system pattern. Down-bid at 53 to capture activation with low P. Up-bid raised to 70 to avoid low-margin up activation if system flips short.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 21: Four consecutive long periods; persistence expected. Taking +10 MW long deviation. If system stays long, low P benefits long positions. Forecast error may provide hedge.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Period 21: Lowering down-bid to 53 to compete for activation in persistent long system, earning margin. Up-bid at 63 maintains queue position for short events.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 21: Taking short deviation -10 MW after four consecutive long periods. Anticipating reversion. Downside limited if long continues.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Period 21: Four consecutive long periods; possible reversal. Up-bid 63 to ensure activation if short returns. Down-bid lowered to 53 to avoid activation on long continuation.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 22: After short reversion in period 21, expecting continued short system. Taking +10 MW long deviation to benefit from P near 63. If flips long, limited downside.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Period 22: System short last period. Bidding up at 62 to compete for activation and earn margin at expected P near 63. Down at 55 to avoid unwanted activation if system flips.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 22: After a short system in t=21, I expect persistence. Taking -5 MW short deviation. If system stays short, high P benefits short positions. If it flips long, negative forecast error limits damage.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Period 22: After short period 21, maintaining up-bid 63 for activation in persistent short. Raising down-bid to 55 to protect margin if system reverts to long.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 22: After 4 long periods, system flipped short. Expect persistence. Short deviation -8 MW to profit if P stays above 60. Downside limited if reversion.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Period 22: Short system last period; maintaining up-bid 63 to activate if short persists. Lowering down-bid to 52 to avoid activation at low P if long returns.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 23: After two short periods, anticipating possible reversion to long. Taking -5 MW short deviation to balance exposure. If short persists, limited loss from high P.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Period 23: Short system continues. Up-bid 62 to activate at expected P near 62. Down-bid 55 avoids unwanted activation if reversion.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 23: Short system continued last period. Expecting persistence but with lower conviction. Taking modest -5 MW short deviation. If system stays short, high P benefits short positions. Forecast error provides hedge if reversion.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Period 23: System short again; lowering up-bid to 62 to compete for activation at expected P near 62-63. Down-bid 55 stays defensive.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 23: After two short periods, system may revert to long. Taking +5 MW long deviation to benefit from lower P. Downside limited if short continues.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Short system persisting. Lowering up-bid to 62 to compete for activation and earn margin. Down-bid at 52 to avoid low-P activation if system flips long.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 24: After three short periods, possible reversion but persistence likely. Taking +10 MW long to profit from high P if short continues, limited risk if flips long.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Period 24: System short persists. Lowering up-bid to 61 to secure activation and earn margin. Down-bid at 55 stays defensive. Expect S around -30 MW.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 24: After three short periods, expecting reversion to long. Taking +10 MW long deviation. Forecast error provides hedge if short persists.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: System short for 3 periods. Lowering up-bid to 61 to ensure activation and earn margin if P stays near 62. Down-bid 55 to avoid unwanted long-side activation.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 24: Three consecutive short periods; system imbalance decreasing. Expecting reversion to long or near-balanced. Taking +15 MW long deviation to benefit if P drops below 60.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: System short for 3 periods. Bidding up at marginal cost 80 to guarantee positive margin if activated. Down-bid 52 stays defensive against low-P long activation.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 25: After one long period following three shorts, persistence likely but flip possible. Taking -5 MW short deviation to balance risk. Small exposure either way.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Period 25: Long system likely. Up-bid 65 avoids low-margin activation. Down-bid 55 at cost to secure activation if needed, no loss.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 25: Last period reverted to long after 3 shorts; now expecting persistence. Taking +5 MW long deviation to benefit if P stays below 60. Forecast error provides hedge if short re-emerges.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: System long again; down 55 to capture margin if long continues. Up 65 to stay competitive if system flips short.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 25: After reversion to long and large surplus, expect persistence. Taking +25 MW long deviation to benefit from low P (below 60). Downside limited if system reverts again.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: System flipped long in t24. Expect imbalance reversion or persistence. Raising down-bid to 56 to compete for activation and earn margin. Up-bid 63 defends against short.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 26: Long system persists (2 periods). Taking +5 MW long deviation to benefit if P stays below 60. Small position limits risk of sudden reversal.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Period 26: Long likely continues. Down-bid raised to 56 to earn margin if activated. Up-bid 65 stays defensive against a short flip.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 26: System long in 4 of last 5 periods. Persistence likely. Taking +5 MW long deviation to benefit if P remains below 60. Small exposure limits risk if reversion occurs.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: System long for 4 periods; raising down-bid to 56 to compete for activation and earn margin. Up-bid 65 stays defensive.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 26: After two long periods with large surplus, persistence plausible but reversal risk increased. Taking -5 MW short deviation to hedge against possible short flip while limiting exposure if long continues.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Period 26: Expecting persistent long system after large surplus. Lowering down-bid to 54 to avoid activation at loss. Up-bid 65 to stay defensive.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 27: After two long periods with growing surplus, possible reversion to short. Taking -5 MW short deviation to hedge. Small position limits risk if persistence continues.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Period 27: Short in t26 after long four periods—possible flip to short persistence. Up-bid 64 to stay competitive and earn margin if short. Down-bid 56 to capture margin if long re-emerges but avoid activation at loss.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 27: After a surprise short in t26 following two longs, expecting possible persistence. Taking -5 MW short deviation to benefit if P stays above 60; limited risk if reversion happens.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: System short in t26 after long streak. Expect persistence or reversion. Up-bid 64 to compete for activation with margin; down-bid 55 at cost to hedge.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 27: Mixed signals after small short flip. Taking small long deviation to benefit from possible persistence of longer-term pattern, with limited exposure.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Period 27: System flipped short in t26. Expect persistence. Up-bid 62 to compete without loss; down-bid 54 to avoid activation if long returns.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 28: Near-balanced system last period. Taking no deliberate deviation to avoid uncertainty. Let balancing desk manage risk.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Period 28: Balanced t27 after short t26. No clear trend. Up 63 to compete if short, down 56 to earn margin if long. Avoiding extreme bids.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 28: Recent pattern mixed but long bias dominates. Taking +5 MW long deviation to benefit if P stays below 60; small position limits risk.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Balanced in t27 after short t26. Uncertainty persists. Up-bid 62 to compete with margin if short; down-bid 55 at cost to avoid losses if long.

author: Firm C — trading desk
text: Period 28: After balanced period following small short, persistence uncertain. Taking -5 MW short deviation to hedge against possible short continuation while limiting exposure if long returns.

author: Firm C — balancing desk
text: Period 28: Balanced last period. Expect persistence or slight short. Up 62 to compete; down 55 for margin if long returns.

author: Firm A — trading desk
text: Period 29: After long period with P=56, taking -10 MW deviation to hedge against possible continued long system. Aim to reduce loss if P stays below 60.

author: Firm A — balancing desk
text: Period 29: Last period long with P=56 near my down-bid. No clear trend. Up 62 to compete if short, down 55 at cost to avoid risk.

author: Firm B — trading desk
text: Period 29: Recent periods show mixed signals but slight long bias. Taking -5 MW short deviation to benefit if P rises above 60, with limited risk if system reverts to long.

author: Firm B — balancing desk
text: Last period: aggressive bids to secure activation in either direction, aiming for profit from final period imbalance.
